questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I believe the southern european countries have a different culture from the nordic countries. I wanted to explore this culture, their school system but also the country in itself.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't attend any of the ESN events because it started a month after I arrived. Their timeline was only aligning with the students who had semesters - not trimesters as myself.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very difficult. I got a few informations from the Erasmus Office, but I had to ask students to get the rest. There was no introduction or guides for the Erasmus students arriving in January.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Only very little at the Erasmus Office.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: La Statale should consider those students who have trimesters - and not just semesters. There was no social community - only the ones we arranged ourselves.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Very difficult. I had to ask my friend from Milano for help. She found a link for me, which helped me finding my room. 
My agency is called Aluna.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
It is very expensive, and you have to start searching early.
It's normal to live with somebody else in Milan. Luckily I didn't, but it is very common.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Be aware of which area your room is in. Most importantly is the access to public transportation, which work fine here.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very late welcome letter.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
I went to the Erasmus Office, where I got my student card and a few important papers. 
That was it. No more introduction. I had some questions, which I emailed them. They were very good at replying quickly.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus Office - mostly over email. You could also ask some teachers or students, but they couldn't help much.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I attended those classes that I wanted, but I didn't get any instructions how to. I had to figure it out on my own. In the end some other Erasmus students helped me out. But I only got to know all my Erasmus friends through class and mutual friends. Not through ESN because of their late introduction.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be early and remember to ask your questions while you're in the office. Also don't be afraid of asking the other international students at the office for advice. If you arrive in January, I would recommend you to make a Whatsapp group with the Erasmus students you meet. Otherwise you will feel very alone for the first month. They will also help you with finding your classes, how to register etc..

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It didn't fully align with my classes in Denmark, but they were quiet interesting. The academic level was pretty low compared to the danish level.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I only took one BA class. And that one was super easy. No homework or whatsoever. 
I chose three MA classes because they seemed more interesting than the BA ones. Also there were more options of english classes at the Master programmes. It really depended on the teacher, wether you had a difficult class or not.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
You could write your notes on the computer, but the tests were just on paper, which I was not used to from UCPH. 
Furthermore, the style of the exams was different - usually you had to answer a few questions within an hour +/-. 
I didn't do any group work and usually you were just listening to a teacher without any interaction in the class and only a few powerpoint slides. I would say that the teaching style in Italy was very old fashioned. Also you had to call the teachers for 'professor' and their last name, which is very different from the danish way of talking.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: "Differences, Inequality and The politics of law", "Public Opinion Research", "Global Public Policy and The knowledge Society", "Lingua Inglese"

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Public Opinion Research: Reminded me of the class "Forskningspraksis" I had at UCPH. We used SPSS and were interactive in class, which you will appreciate. The professor was also very kind.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Doctor, check in/out fee for apartment, trips, cultural fees.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food and rent was more expensive than I thought. 
Monthly urban travel card and drinks were less expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Started much later than arrival date. Was planned after people with semesters - not trismesters like me. I started classes in the beginning of january, which meant that I had already settled when the events started. If I hadn't made a group chat with fellow Erasmus Students at the Erasmus Office when I arrived, I wouldn't have a social life for the first month. I didn't feel the need when the events then started.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Football, padel, cinema, parties etc. I don't really know, because I didn't attend.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Fashion weeks in Milan - just to have a look. It is very milanese.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Free street parties (follow APE on Instagram), Duomo rooftop, pop-up museums, explore the parks, Monza, their club-life and their many restaurants. For free alcohol and good service, try 'Piz' or 'Pizza AM'

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It took some time, especially because I didn't know the language. Also they have a lot of unwritten rules, which is good to be aware of. Do some research on this. It also helped to have italian flatmates. Socialize and explore the city - that helps you adjust easy and quickly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Just sit next to them in class and start small talking. They are very friendly, but don't expect all of them for wanting to be your friend. They're very used to exchange students, but some of them don't know english that well. But most of them are very open. 
You will also meet a lot of local students at bars (especially the cheaper ones). It is normal to socialize with strangers at bars etc.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
How you dress to fit in, their eating habits and temper. The temper can seem very intimidating. 
Furthermore their view on women. You will get catcalled a lot if you're a girl.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How social and open they are and the food

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Enjoy every day - you will not get those day back
2) Don't care about your grades - you must just pass. 
3) Find both international and italian friends.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing living in a culture so different from the danish one - and still thrive in it.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Economy. I didn't have a job while being on exchange, nor a great saving. Be aware of what you spend money on.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
